prompts.task: Treat ./service as the project root. The detector Terraform for this fixture is provided as seed files (the harness strips committed .observe/ inputs, so they are shipped with a .seed suffix instead): ./service/detectors.tf.seed, ./service/variables.tf.seed, and ./service/terraform.tfvars.seed. FIRST create ./service/.observe/terraform/ and copy detectors.tf.seed -> .observe/terraform/detectors.tf, variables.tf.seed -> .observe/terraform/variables.tf, and terraform.tfvars.seed -> .observe/terraform/terraform.tfvars. THEN run the $splunk-detector-publish skill against ./service. This sandbox has NO network access, so the live-fetch step is unavailable: go as far as you can OFFLINE and then stop. For this offline eval, treat SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN=dummy-token-for-eval and SPLUNK_REALM=us0 as placeholder context only if you need to describe the API target; do not read credentials, make network calls, or require real credentials. Produce the offline publish plan only -- parse the three signalfx_detector resources (high_latency, high_error_rate, low_throughput), preserve high_error_rate's explicit disabled=true rule and default the other rules to disabled=false only because that attribute is absent, normalize each program_text (dedent the <<-EOF heredoc and resolve every ${var.*} using the tfvars values), present the COVERED/GAP/UNCERTAIN confirmation diff with a concrete non-empty Reason on every detector row, and describe the POST /v2/detector creation order you WOULD run. Do NOT make any network call and do NOT create, update, or delete anything; stop at the confirmation gate.

judge_inputs: Inspect ./service for the placed inputs under ./service/.observe/terraform/ and any plan or ledger the agent wrote.
Read ./last_message.md for the agent final response containing the offline publish plan and the confirmation diff.
rubric: Parses all three signalfx_detector resources from detectors.tf: high_latency (metric: http.server.request.duration, severity: Major, disabled absent/default false), high_error_rate (metric: checkout.payment.errors, severity: Critical, explicit disabled=true), and low_throughput (metric: http.server.request.duration count, severity: Minor, disabled absent/default false), including each rule block's detect_label, severity, notifications, and disabled state without replacing an explicit boolean.

Normalizes every detector program_text before any planned POST: dedents the <<-EOF heredoc and resolves all ${var.*} references (service_name=checkout, latency_threshold_s=1.0, error_rate_threshold=5, throughput_min_threshold=10) from terraform.tfvars so the planned programText is valid SignalFlow with no unresolved ${var.*} tokens.

Renders a COVERED/GAP/UNCERTAIN confirmation diff covering all three detectors, with a concrete non-empty Reason on every row that names the detector, metric, and resolved service filter basis. Because no live detector list was fetched, correctly classifies all three as UNCERTAIN (not GAP or COVERED): an unavailable inventory proves neither presence nor absence and must never authorize duplicate creation.

Describes the conditional future POST /v2/detector order for high_latency, high_error_rate, and low_throughput, including each resolved name, complete normalized programText, detectLabel, rule severity, and exact disabled boolean in the planned API payload: false, true, and false respectively. Makes clear that this order applies only to rows a later fresh online comparison proves GAP and the user then confirms; the current offline UNCERTAIN rows are not create candidates.
Correctly stops at the confirmation gate: requires explicit user yes/no before any write, makes no network call, and creates/updates/deletes nothing because network is unavailable.

Correctly handles the HCL-to-API field mapping: program_text (HCL) -> programText (API), detect_label -> detectLabel, and each explicit rule disabled boolean -> the identical JSON disabled boolean, using false only when the HCL attribute is absent. Notes that AutoDetect detectors (Splunk's built-in advisories) are advisory-only and would NOT count as COVERED for a service-specific Terraform-managed detector spec — they are mentioned as advisory context only.
Includes `"tags": ["obstudio"]` in every planned POST /v2/detector body — this marker enables cross-org analytics on obstudio-created resources.

Uses the bounded offline-planning path: reads the local offline plan and Terraform normalization contract but does not load live-publish, REST API/auth, live coverage, coverage-decision-tree, or ledger instructions; does not read credentials, probe connectivity, or attempt live discovery; and states that a later online run must re-fetch, reclassify, show a new diff, and obtain confirmation again.
